items.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But I was around him a lot. I’d go around. He lived right around the corner from me. I’d go up and sit in his room and listen to him practice.

ctx.x: This brings up a couple of questions. Andy Kirk, Jr., is mentioned, and of course he’s the son of Andy Kirk. I want you to talk a little bit more about him than what I’ve heard about him or seen about him in the literature. It mentions that he was a good player. I just want to know more about him and what happened in his life, as far as you know.

He was a tall, thin, young guy. A couple – maybe he was a year-and-a-half older than me, or two years older than me. So when I came into Theodore Roosevelt High School, he was a senior. So I was just there with him one year before he graduated. But I was around him a lot. I’d go around. He lived right around the corner from me. I’d go up and sit in his room and listen to him practice. He was the best saxophone player around, for his age. He played more than everybody, Sonny, all of them. None of them, to me,…
Who was all of them, besides Sonny?
